milestone_scope: m1 (seed world) and m2 (checkpoint/diff): `up` provisions the bundled postgres-starter world and records its manifest; `status` prints services plus the seeded-state fingerprint; `checkpoint <label>` snapshots the world; `diff <label>` reports the filesystem and row mutations since it. `run` (m3) is a roadmap stub.
prerequisites: worldcheck binary: go build ./cmd/worldcheck (or go install github.com/SuperMarioYL/worldcheck/cmd/worldcheck@latest)
scenario: Provision the bundled seeded test world, checkpoint it before verification, let an agent bend one seeded row and drop one file to force its own test green, and read back the mutation diff — then edit seed.sql and re-provision to show the fingerprint move (the m1 acceptance criterion).

verification: go test ./... — unit tests (fake runner, no daemon) plus the real-world integration tests TestProvisionRealPostgresStarterWorld, TestProvisionRealWorldWithoutHealthcheck and TestCheckpointAndDiffRealWorld, which run against a real Docker daemon; unit tests stay green with -short.

The integration tests provision the same seed twice and require identical fingerprints, then edit seed.sql and require the fingerprint to change; provision a world whose compose file has no healthcheck; and require the checkpoint/diff pair to report exactly one updated row after the agent bends one.
A schema-only seed edit (appending CREATE INDEX) was also run by hand and moves the fingerprint, which the v0.1 --data-only capture could not do.
limitations: m3 (`run` with the pass-plus-mutations reconciliation report and worldcheck.html) is a stub: the command exists and prints the roadmap note instead of executing.

The filesystem half of a diff reports what `docker diff` sees, which includes the container's own runtime paths (a live Postgres rewrites /tmp and its data directory). The row deltas are the precise signal; the filesystem list is the raw container view.

The committed GIF is a frame sequence rendered from this real recorded run (this machine's vhs cannot complete an encode); docs/demo.tape plus docs/demo-record.sh produce a true terminal recording where vhs works.
Windows is out of scope; macOS and Linux are supported.
